entries.title: Jeremiah 46:1
segments: The word of the Lord--against the Gentiles; here begins a series of prophecies against the heathen nations, extending through the remainder of the book, with the exception of the last chapter.  The present verse constitutes a preface to the whole series.

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:2
segments: Against Egypt; that is, as immediately explained, against Pharaoh's expedition against the Chaldees.  He made two expeditions against Carchemish; in the first of these he slew Josiah,

, and afterwards defeated the Chaldeans and took the city; in the second, his army was defeated with great loss, as here predicted. 
 
Nations that know not God are subject to his providential control.  He makes all their movements subservient to the interests of his church, exalting one to power and overthrowing another, according to his pleasure.

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:3
segments: Order ye the buckler; addressed to the Egyptians, as much as to say, All your preparations for war shall end in your own destruction.

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:4
segments: Get up, ye horsemen; go up against Assyria.

But many render, "Mount, ye horsemen." 
 
  Brigandines; coats of mail.

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:5
segments:
vv 5-6. 
 
  Wherefore have I seen--they shall stumble and fal; the prophet sees in vision the terror and flight of the Egyptians by the Euphrates. 
 
When God fights against a people, no array of human might can avail; he will turn all its plans for conquering others to its own destruction.

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:7
segments:
vv 7-8. 
 
  Who is this--will cover the earth; the prophet returns now to the preparations of the Egyptians.  He compares their vast armies to the overflowing waters of the Nile.

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:9
segments: Lydians; here probably an African tribe.  Compare

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:10
segments:
The day of the Lord God of hosts; when he gathers together the armies of Egypt to destroy them. 
 
  A sacrifice; a great slaughter of the Egyptians. 
 
  In the north country; in the land of the Chaldeans.  See note on

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:11
segments: Gilead; the land of balm.
The meaning is, Though thou gather the balm of Gilead, thou canst not be healed of thy wounds.

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:13
segments: The word that the Lord spake; these words introduce a second prophecy against Egypt, referring to the invasion of the land by Nebuchadnezzar, which took place some years after Pharaoh-necho's disastrous expedition against the Chaldees.

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:14
segments: Stand fast--prepare thee; a mighty conqueror is coming: let Egypt prepare to resist him, if she can.

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:16
segments: They said; the hired troops of the Egyptians.

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:17
segments:
There; in the land of their nativity, after their return home. 
 
  Passed; that is, has let pass. 
 
  The time appointed; or, the set time.  By this, some understand the time set for meeting and sustaining his allies; others, the opportunity of success. 
 
Since all the power of kings and rulers comes from God, none of them can shield transgressors against his wrath.  Sinners who confide in their promises of help, will find them to be "but a noise" without substance.

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:18
segments: As Tabor--as Carmel--shall he come; Nebuchadnezzar shall come with the strength and majesty of Tabor and Carmel, the two most prominent mountains in north Palestine.

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:19
segments: Daughter dwelling in Egypt; Egypt is personified as a delicate female.

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:21
segments: Her hired men; see note on

. 
 
  Like fatted bullocks; they are well fed and lusty, but flee in wild confusion before the enemy.

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:22
segments:
The voice thereof; literally, "her voice," Egypt's voice. 
 
  Shall go like a serpent; as a serpent retreats with hissing and terror before the woodman. 
 
  Against her; against Egypt.

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:23
segments:
Her forest; her armies and people. 
 
  Though it cannot be searched; though its trees are of vast extent and innumerable.

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:25
segments: No; the celebrated capital of Egypt, in Upper Egypt, on both sides of the Nile.

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:26
segments: Afterward it shall be inhabited; the desolation of Egypt by Nebuchadnezzar was only temporary.  Compare

entries.title: Jeremiah 46:27
segments:
vv 27-28. 
 
The nations of the world rise to power and perish in rapid succession; but in the midst of all thise changes, God's kingdom is continually advancing under his own immediate superintendence.  All the afflictions which befall his people have the effect, not to destroy, but to purify them, and thus prepare them for increased prosperity.
